question.text: Ferdinand and his wife were assassinated by this 19-year old Yugoslav nationalist. He was a member of the Black Hand, which planned Franz Ferdinand's assassination.
question.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

swap.text: In this nation, the Gorbachev administration transferred power to Ion Iliescu [ill-YES-koo] after the revolt against, and public execution of, Nicolae Ceausescu [choh-SHESS-koo].
swap.clue: After Decree 770 all but banned contraception and abortion here, abusive orphanages such as Cighid filled with babies.

question.text: This former president of Yugoslavia was put on trial for crimes against humanity, but he died during the proceedings at the Hague. He allegedly committed genocide in Kosovo.
question.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

swap.leadin: A country is not actually a country until the United Nations officially recognizes it. Identify these "wannabe" nations.
swap.text: With its capital at Pristina and a population of mostly Albanians, it declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Russia blocked its recognition with a veto.
swap.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

question.leadin: Answer the following about twentieth-century political unrest that happened in June.
question.text: The June Revolution in this country exiled its last king and brought Prime Minister Fan Noli to power. A later leader of this country, Enver Hoxha ("HOE-zhuh"), improved relations with Mao Zedong amidst the Sino-Soviet split.
question.answerHtml: Albania [or Republic of Albania or Republika e Shqiperise or Shqiperia]
question.clue: Its port-city of Vlore was the site of its proclamation of independence, as well as the site of major riots after this country's economy collapsed from a gigantic system of Ponzi schemes.

swap.leadin: This region names two wars fought by a namesake league at the start of the 20th century, which involved Austrian intervention and Russian support.
swap.text: Name this region, the "powder keg of Europe," where Otto von Bismarck predicted the next European war would begin. A war ending in 1878 had ensured the independence of most of its states from a declining empire.
swap.clue: Alexander Stamboliyski was assassinated by IMRO, which advocated for a state in this peninsula.

question.text: As a result of the last Russo-Turkish War, this country gained autonomy from Ottoman rule. Boris III was a tsar of this modern-day nation, whose capital city is Sofia.
question.clue: This country pursued the Treaty of Craiova to recover territory lost in the Treaty of Neuilly, its "second national catastrophe," which saw it lose Southern Dobruja.

swap.leadin: Basil II had the longest reign of any leader of his empire, revitalizing it over his nearly 50-year rule.
swap.text: Basil is known as the "slayer" of this ethnic group for ending their first empire at the Battle of Kleidion in 1014 and having 99 of every 100 prisoners fully blinded and the remaining left with one eye.
swap.answerHtml: Bulgars [do not accept or prompt on “Bulgarians,” as that is a distinct modern ethnic group]
swap.clue: The Paulicians may have inspired a Gnostic, dualistic sect which arose among these people called Bogomilism.

question.text: Former capitals of this region include Campulung and Curtea de Arges. Distinct from the mountainous Transylvania, for 15 points, name this region that contains Bucharest, and that united with Moldavia to form Romania.
question.clue: This region was the first one to be ruled by Michael the Brave.

swap.leadin: One of this man's epithets derives from his father's membership in the Order of the Dragon.
swap.text: Identify this voivode of Wallachia who led the Night Attack against Mehmed II in 1462. He was captured by Matthias Corvinus of Hungary later that year.
swap.answerHtml: Vlad III Dracula [or Vlad the Impaler or Vlad Tepes or Vlad Dracula; prompt on Dracula; prompt on Vlad; do not accept or prompt on "Vlad Dracul"]
swap.clue: This brother of Radu the Handsome repelled an advance by troops under Mehmet II in the Night Attack.

question.leadin: This man declared that mothers of at least ten children were "heroine mothers."
question.text: Name this Communist leader executed along with his wife Elena on Christmas Day, 1989. He replaced Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej as General Secretary of his country's Communist Party in 1965.
question.clue: Thousands of orphans were crammed into orphanages such as Cighid during this man's reign.

swap.leadin: At the end of the second of these conflicts, one of the countries involved ceded territory in the Treaty of Bucharest and the Treaty of Constantinople.

swap.clue: The first of these was ended by the Treaty of London, though it left the possession of Salonika and Thrace unresolved.

question.text: Benedetto Cotrugli, an economist from this city, described an early version of double-entry bookkeeping. This city became a major maritime republic after being transferred from Venice to Hungary in the Treaty of Zadar.
question.clue: The nobles of this city elected its leaders to a position known as either Rector or knez ("k'nez").

swap.text: After the War of Chioggia, Venice lost control of Ragusa, which later became a major trading republic in this region. To repay its debt to Venice, the Fourth Crusade sacked Zadar, a city in this region on the eastern Adriatic coast.

question.text: In 1918, Peter I's kingdom expanded to form Yugoslavia, composed of Serbs, Croats, and this ethnic group. This ethnic group's namesake republic, which includes Melania Trump's birthplace in Novo Mesto, was the first country to break from Yugoslavia in 1990.
question.clue: Amidst the Germanisation of Carinthia in the High Middle Ages, this language remained in use in several areas, and in investiture until 1597. This Slavic language was also spoken in neighbouring Carniola, home to Ljubljana ("lyoob-LYAH-nuh").

swap.leadin: The Treaty of San Stefano prompted Abdyl Frasheri to lead the League of Prizren in resistance against the partition of lands inhabited by this ethnic group.
swap.text: Name these people whose first prime minister Ismail Qemali waved the flag from the Assembly of Vlore ("VLAW-ruh") after declaring independence in 1912.
swap.clue: A fighter for these people named George Kastrioti took a title meaning "Lord Alexander" in Turkish; that national hero was Skanderbeg.

question.leadin: The organization headed by this man carried out a reign of terror in the 1930s that included the Velebit Uprising and it responded to King Alexander I's challenge to kill him by doing just that.
question.text: Name this leader of the Ustase movement, who used that position to persecute Jews, Serbs and Roma in concentration camps like Jasenovac.

question.leadin: Note to players: description acceptable. In 1990, millions of supporters of this cause made a "Bridge of Flowers" by throwing petals into the Prut River.
question.text: Name this cause that aims to recreate a short-lived polity formed in 1918 by a proclamation of the Sfatul Tarii ("s'FAH-tool TSUH-ree"). Mircea ("MEER-ch'yah") Snegur's opposition to this cause prompted him to leave the Moldovan Popular Front in 1991.
